This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 05.06.2023 at about 11.00 a.m. he had been riding Activa Honda bearing Reg. No.KA-02-JC- 5814 on Kengeri - Tavarekere Road, near Kommaghatta,
Sulikere, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, at that time, a Luggage Auto bearing Reg.
No.KA-41-B-0619 came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against his vehicle,
as a result of which, petitioner sustained grievous injuries and his vehicle was also damaged badly.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Sanyra Hospital and Diagnostic, Bengaluru for initial treatment, thereafter shifted to BGS Gleneagles Global Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and spent a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, medicines,
conveyance, nourishing food and attendant charges.
SCCH-5 3.

At the time of the accident he was aged about 26 years, hale and healthy, working as Executive - Marketing at BGS Gleneagles Global Hospital, thereby earning Rs.35,024/- p.m., due to this accident he became permanently disable, unable to do his day-to-day activities.
Out of this accident crime No.200/2023 is registered against the driver of the said luggage auto before the Kumbalagudu Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 is insurer of the said offending vehicle.
Respondent No.2 is deleted as per court order dated 06.07.2024.
Respondent No.1 being the R.C.Owner is liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. SCCH-5 4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer has appeared through counsel and petition against respondent No.2 is deleted as per court order dated 06.07.2024.

Ltd., as PW-3 and Dr.B.Ramesh, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW-4 and marked 25 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.25 and closed his evidence.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, the points that would arise for my consideration are:
::POINTS::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 05.06.2023 at about 11.00 a.m. when he was riding Activa Honda bearing Reg. No.KA-02-J-5814 on Kengeri - Tavarekere Road, near Kommagatta Sulikere, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru Sourth Taluk, at that time, one Luggage Auto bearing Reg. No.KA- 41-B-0619 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
SCCH-5 8.

Then my findings on the above points are as follows:
Point No.1 : In the Affirmative Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order for the following:

::REASONS::
9. Point No.1:- In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is SCCH-5 marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.6.
10.
Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined Medical Record Incharge and Manager at Gleneagles BGS Hospital and Doctor PW-1 to PW-3.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 Sanjay .S.V vs Mohammed Shahabuddin on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80676131/

11.
Per contra, respondent No.1 has placed exparte.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 05.06.2023 at about 11.00 a.m. when SCCH-5 he was riding Honda Activa bearing Reg. No.KA-02-JC- 5814 on Kengeri - Tavarekere Road, near Kommaghatta, Sulikere,
Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the Luggage Auto bearing Reg. No.KA-41-B-0619.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above point No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Point No.1 in the affirmative.
SCCH-5 13. Point No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained moderate traumatic brain injury, bifrontal contusions with active right subdural - hemorrhage, comminuted displaced fractures in lateral femoral condyle, fractures in posterior intracondylar region of tibia and fracture in lateral facet of patella, for the said injuries he took treatment in the form of internal fixation of femur and tibia.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7,
discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by BGS Gleneagles Global Hospital, Kengeri,
Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 05.06.2023 to 23.06.2023.

Further he has furnished OPD Record marked as Ex.P.9, medical bills for a sum of Rs.6,365/- marked as Ex.P.10 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.11.

15.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited OPD Book marked as Ex.P.24 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.25 and he has assessed permanent physical disability of 36% of right lower limb, which is 18%
of whole body.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation SCCH-5 reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 12% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 36% of lower limb disability, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Bengaluru, thereby drawing salary of Rs.35,024/- p.m.

To prove the said fact, petitioner has examined Manager - HR at Gleneagles BGS Hospital as PW-3 and exhibited copy of payslips for the month of March to May marked as Ex.P.22 and copy of final settlement statement marked as Ex.P.23.

So as per Ex.P.22 payslips for the month of May 2023, petitioner has earned Rs.35,028/-
i.e., just prior to the accident month and said document is exhibited by PW-3.

Hence notional income of the petitioner is taken into consideration as Rs.35,028/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.
SCCH-5
It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8, petitioner was admitted in BGS Gleneagles Global Hospital as inpatient from 05.06.2023 to 23.06.2023 i.e., for 18 days.

For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income as per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.35,028/- p.m.

SCCH-5 19
. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.10 medical bills for Rs.63,625/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.7 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 05.06.2023.

So as per Ex.P.7 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained comminuted fracture of right lateral femoral condyle, fracture of right tibial plateau, fracture of right patella, right FTP SDH, bilateral frontal lobes hamorrhagic contusions, bilateral hemmrohage, facture of right frontal bone, fracture parietal bones, fracture of right femoral bone, which are grievous in nature.

Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Nandish N.P. and respondent No.1 R.C.Owner of the offending vehicle the SCCH-5 offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC and Sec.196 of M.V.Act.

For the reasons assigned to points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,87,127/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Eighty Seven Thousand One Hundred Twenty Seven Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
